finding.expected: Bind failure ownership explicitly to the current remediation attempt rather than inferring it from repository-global RUN-directory differences. Before a RUN is created, any failure from this remediation must remain an ADMISSION_FAILURE regardless of concurrent RUN creation. After this remediation creates its own RUN, only that exact RUN may be sent through the existing RUN-keyed FAILURE path. Add a deterministic concurrency/race regression proving a foreign RUN cannot be claimed or suppress the current admission diagnostic, without adding retries or another Executor call.
finding.issue: Pre-RUN versus post-RUN ownership is inferred by taking a repository-global snapshot of runtime RUN filenames before _run_remediation_impl and then comparing the directory again after an exception. That inference is not bound to the current remediation attempt. If another process creates a RUN after this call takes its initial snapshot but before this call fails admission (for example while the other process holds RepositoryLock), the foreign RUN appears in `created`. The wrapper can then call _persist_and_transport_failure against that unrelated active RUN instead of emitting ADMISSION_FAILURE for the current rejected remediation. Conversely, another RUN created immediately after this remediation's own post-RUN failure can make `created` contain more than one item and suppress terminal failure persistence altogether. This makes admission observability race-dependent and can corrupt RUN failure lineage even though the current remediation never invoked an Executor.
